title: The Pirahã — a language with no numbers, no past tense
voiceover: Deep in the Amazon, there's a tribe of about 800 people called the Pirahã. Their language has no numbers. No past tense. No word for color. No creation myth. They don't have words for one, two, or three — just words that roughly mean some, many, and lots. They live almost entirely in the present moment. A linguist named Daniel Everett spent over 30 years with them, trying to convert them to Christianity. He ended up so changed by them, he abandoned his religion and his career. Their language broke a major theory of human linguistics. They just didn't fit our rules. Follow Mindbloom for one fact a day.
